learning_outcome: The student will be able to identify and match identical geometric shapes and colors.
student_action: Match the shape on the left column with its identical counterpart in the right column by drawing a line.
visual_elements: Two vertical columns of colorful geometric shapes (blue circle, purple diamond, green square, yellow star, red heart) separated by dots. The shapes are simple, solid-colored icons with black outlines.
scaffolding_details: No explicit scaffolding or examples provided; relies entirely on visual cues.
prior_knowledge_required: Basic recognition of primary/secondary colors and basic geometric shapes.
common_misconceptions: Matching based on color only while ignoring shape (e.g., if there were two different blue shapes)
Difficulty with spatial orientation when drawing lines
teacher_guidance: Since there are no written instructions, the teacher must verbally instruct the child to 'find the same shape' and 'draw a line to connect them'. Use this to assess if the child can distinguish between shape and color.
adaptation_suggestions: For struggling learners: Provide a physical example by drawing the first line. For advanced learners: Ask them to name the shape and color aloud after matching.
reasoning: The worksheet contains two columns of shapes with dots in between, which is a standard visual convention for matching tasks. The shapes are clearly identifiable (circle, diamond, square, star, heart) and the task is unambiguous for the target age group.
